answer: Reputation-weighted escrow curve: each new identity must post collateral set by a concave curve of its verified interaction history, starting at a steep summit and flattening as reputation accrues. Collateral is slashed only after adjudicated fraud, and released on a schedule tied to a sable trust score. An attacker on an isolated island of fresh identities pays roughly the square of N in locked capital to sustain N concurrent sybils, since none inherit history. Cost scales superlinearly with fleet size; honest single agents amortize collateral over repeated honest trades.
